# Report tables: new approach P1-P3 (generated by make_report_tables.py; do not edit by hand)

Source: Colab run New_approach_done.ipynb, NVIDIA L4, seed 42, one run. Files: final_model_results/.

All numbers are on the official test set unless the table says dev. Raw results come first; calibrated second.

## Terms

- P1: crop_b1 + disease_b1. P2: crop_b1 + disease_clip. P3: crop = mean of crop_b1 and crop_clip; disease = mean of disease_clip and disease_small_reg (means of log-probabilities).

- Pair score = log P(crop) + r x log P(disease) - gamma x [pair seen in training]. Raw results use gamma = 0 and r = 1.

- gamma: a penalty taken off every seen pair so that unseen pairs can win. r: the weight of the disease score.

- Augmentation "b1": random crop 224 (area 85-100%), horizontal and vertical flip, rotation +-10 degrees, brightness and contrast +-0.15 (the Baseline 1 recipe). "strong": crop area 30-100%, flips, TrivialAugmentWide, random erasing (p 0.25).

## Table 1. Training settings of the five models

All models: AdamW, cross-entropy loss, cosine learning-rate decay (stage 1 T_max 30, stage 2 T_max 10), no warm-up, mixed precision, 224 x 224 input. Stage 1: dev split (6,905 train images), max 25 epochs, early stop after 5 epochs with no better dev HM (seen and unseen Top-1 of the model's own task), keep the best dev epoch. Stage 2: 10 epochs on all 8,000 training images from the best stage-1 weights; keep the epoch with the best train accuracy. Test: average of the image and its mirror image (flip). CLIP models use CLIP's own image normalisation.

| Model | Task | Backbone | Augmentation | Head | Stage 1 lr (backbone / head) | Stage 2 lr (backbone / head) | Weight decay | Label smoothing | Stochastic depth | Batch | Seed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| crop_b1 | crop | convnext_tiny | b1 | dropout 0.3 + linear 768->N | 1e-05 / 0.001 | 1e-06 / 0.0001 | 0.001 | 0.0 | 0.1 (torchvision default) | 16 | 42 |
| crop_clip | crop | clip_vit_b16 | b1 | frozen CLIP text prompts, cosine x learned scale | 1e-05 / 0.001 | 1e-06 / 0.0001 | 0.1 | 0.0 | none | 16 | 42 |
| disease_b1 | disease | convnext_tiny | b1 | dropout 0.2 + linear 768->N | 1e-05 / 0.001 | 1e-06 / 0.0001 | 0.001 | 0.0 | 0.1 (torchvision default) | 16 | 42 |
| disease_clip | disease | clip_vit_b16 | b1 | frozen CLIP text prompts, cosine x learned scale | 1e-05 / 0.001 | 1e-06 / 0.0001 | 0.1 | 0.0 | none | 16 | 42 |
| disease_small_reg | disease | convnext_small | strong | dropout 0.2 + linear 768->N | 1e-05 / 0.001 | 1e-06 / 0.0001 | 0.05 | 0.1 | 0.4 | 16 | 42 |

Baseline 1 values come from the team Baseline 1 notebook; its HM here is recomputed from its rounded seen and unseen values (the Baseline 1 notebook prints pair HM 11.90 for Top-1 and 30.80 for Top-5). P1 retrains the Baseline 1 recipe (the same ConvNeXt-Tiny models and settings). It differs in three ways: flip averaging at test (Baseline 1 has none); stage 1 stops early (max 25 epochs, patience 5), where Baseline 1 ran 30 epochs with no early stop; and the GPU (NVIDIA L4 here, Tesla T4 for Baseline 1).

The 333-pair list is the 323 training pairs plus the 10 unseen test pairs (closed-world setting). Calibrated results use this list, so they assume the 10 possible new pairs are known. Rule 1 was named the main calibrated result before the test was run.

Read the calibrated unseen numbers with care. In 8 of the 10 unseen pairs, the crop has only one unseen pair in the list (cucumber has two). So crop accuracy caps calibrated unseen pair accuracy. With rule 2 and in the reference row, unseen pair accuracy is within 2 points of unseen crop accuracy, because the model only has to pick the crop's one unseen pair over its seen pairs, not one of 175 diseases. With rule 1 the gap is larger (for example P3: 74.86 pair against 84.74 crop).

Computed by paper_metrics.py from the saved log-probabilities (checks: check_paper_metrics.py). It follows the reporting idea of the CZSL papers (TMN, CGE, CompCos): gamma is swept from "always a seen pair" to "always an unseen pair". Here the sweep visits every distinct operating point; public CZSL evaluation code samples a smaller set of bias values, which can give slightly lower best HM and AUC (a few tenths of a point on our scores). Best seen, best unseen and best HM are each the best point of the sweep on the split shown, so on test they are optimistic and are not a model or gamma choice. Table 3 holds the raw results (gamma = 0) and Table 5 the results with gamma fixed on dev before the test. AUC is the area under the seen-against-unseen accuracy curve, in % of the unit square.

Open-world best seen equals closed-world best seen, and is higher than the raw seen value of Table 3: at the "always a seen pair" end only the seen pairs compete (323 on test, 313 on dev), in both worlds. Closed-world best unseen equals the reference row of Table 5, and like it is capped by crop accuracy, because in 8 of the 10 unseen pairs the crop has only one unseen pair in the list (see the note under Table 5). Published benchmarks have many more unseen pairs (for example MIT-States, UT-Zappos, C-GQA), so our closed-world AUC is not comparable with theirs; the open-world rows are the harder setting. The dev rows come from the stage-1 models on the dev pair list (313 seen + 10 hidden pairs), not from the stage-2 models used on test.

## Points the report must state

- One seed (42) and one run, so there are no error bars. Gaps of 1-3 points between phases may be noise.

- The main comparison with Baseline 1 is Table 3 / Table 4 (all 9,625 pairs). Calibrated results (Table 5) use the closed-world 333-pair list, and their unseen accuracy is capped by crop recognition (see the note under Table 5).

- tomato_early_blight is the largest unseen pair (32.6% of unseen images) and P3 gets 0.42% of it right, so it pulls the unseen score down. Most correct unseen pairs (94 of 135) are pepper_bell_bacterial_spot. The unseen score rests on only 10 pairs; the 3 largest hold 66.5% of unseen images.

- On test, calibration rule 1 lowered seen pair accuracy by more than the 3-point dev limit in all three phases (Table 5, against the "Raw, 333-pair list" row: P1 -3.65, P2 -3.80, P3 -5.50 points). Gamma was chosen with the stage-1 models on dev, but the test uses the stage-2 models, which were trained again on all 8,000 images, so the dev limit does not carry over exactly.

- Gamma for this run was fixed on dev before the test labels were read. But the P2 and P3 designs came from earlier runs that were scored on the same official test set (P5 had the P2 design; P6 had the P3 design, pair Top-1 70.95 seen / 10.01 unseen). So the test is not fully untouched by design choices.

- Report rule 1 and rule 2; do not pick one by its test score.

- The brief needs two baselines. These tables compare with Baseline 1 only; Baseline 2 (multi-task CNN) results must be added.
